title: Change a connection when a part stops being part of the whole
body:
Some parts move under one kind of connection and then under another, because the part stops being a part of what it was attached to.

A screw lid on a jar is the clearest case. While it is screwed on, the lid moves along a helical screw axis relative to the jar. Once the thread disengages, the lid is no longer part of the jar: it can be lifted off and moved freely. Other examples:

- a bottle cap unscrewed and then taken off;
- a drawer pulled past its stop and taken out of the cabinet;
- a door lifted off its hinges;
- a cover that slides along a rail and then comes away.

Today a connection is fixed once it is in the world, and estimating a connection from observed poses assumes one kind for the whole motion. Such a motion fits no single kind. The estimator can at best report that nothing explains it.

The idea: a change of the part-whole relationship, such as the lid ceasing to be part of the jar, is what changes the connection. The world would model the lid as connected to the jar by a helical connection while the part-whole relationship holds, and by a free (6-DoF) connection, or a connection to whatever holds it, once the relationship ends. An estimator could then split an observed motion where the relationship changes, and fit each piece on its own.

Open questions:

- Where the part-whole relationship lives: in the semantic annotations, the kinematic structure, or both, and which one is the source of truth.
- What triggers the change: a limit of the connection (the end of the thread), an observation, or an action that is known to detach the part.
- How a change is recorded, published and rolled back, since it replaces a connection rather than changing state.
- Whether the observed poses can tell where the change happened, or whether it has to be given.
